method_card.title: How to Use Pythagoras & SOHCAHTOA
steps: Label the sides: hypotenuse (longest, opposite the right angle), then opposite and adjacent relative to the angle.
Two sides and no angle: use Pythagoras. An angle is involved: use SOHCAHTOA.
Substitute into the formula and solve: square root for Pythagoras, or inverse trig for an angle.
method_card.content:
Pythagoras: in a right-angled triangle \(a^2 + b^2 = c^2\), where \(c\) is the hypotenuse (longest side, opposite the right angle). To find the hypotenuse, \(c = \sqrt{a^2 + b^2}\); to find a shorter side, subtract: \(a = \sqrt{c^2 - b^2}\).

SOHCAHTOA links an angle to two sides: \(\sin\theta = \frac{O}{H}\), \(\cos\theta = \frac{A}{H}\), \(\tan\theta = \frac{O}{A}\). To find a side, rearrange; to find an angle, use \(\sin^{-1}\), \(\cos^{-1}\) or \(\tan^{-1}\). Keep the calculator in degrees.
method_card.example:
Find the hypotenuse of a right triangle with sides 5 cm and 12 cm.

\(c = \sqrt{5^2 + 12^2} = \sqrt{25 + 144} = \sqrt{169} = 13\) cm

gold.display: Diagram not drawn accuratelyFrom the top of a 25 m cliff, the angle of depression to a boat is 35°. How far is the boat from the base of the cliff? Give to 1 d.p.

misconceptions.message: You multiplied: 25 × tan35° ≈ 17.5. The height is opposite and the distance is adjacent, and the height is known, so DIVIDE: d = 25 ÷ tan35° ≈ 35.7 m.

gold.hint: The height is opposite and the distance is adjacent, so distance = 25 ÷ tan35°.

guided_steps.say: The angle of depression from the top equals the angle of elevation at the boat, 35°. The height (25 m) is opposite that angle and the distance is adjacent, so tan35° = 25 ÷ distance, which rearranges to distance = 25 ÷ tan35°.

guided_steps.hint: Divide 25 by tan35°, keeping full accuracy.

guided_steps.pre: Check: 35.7 × tan35°, to the nearest whole number =
guided_steps.done: That returns the 25 m height, so the boat is 35.7 m away.

gold.hint: Halve the base first, then the height, half-base and equal side form a right triangle.

guided_steps.hint: The height splits the base into two equal halves.

guided_steps.pre: The equal side is the hypotenuse: 10² =

gold.display: Diagram not drawn accuratelyFind the diagonal of a cuboid with dimensions 3 cm × 4 cm × 12 cm.

misconceptions.message: You found only the base diagonal: √(3² + 4²) = 5. The space diagonal uses all three edges: √(3² + 4² + 12²) = √169 = 13 cm.

gold.hint: Use all three dimensions: square root of 3 squared plus 4 squared plus 12 squared.

guided_steps.hint: What number times itself makes 169? Try 13.

guided_steps.done: 169 matches 9 + 16 + 144, so the diagonal is 13 cm.

problem_bank.bronze_description: Put the given numbers straight into one formula: square, add or subtract and root for Pythagoras, or multiply by a given sine or cosine for a side.
problem_bank.silver_description: Decide the method first, then rearrange it: choose Pythagoras or the right trig ratio, substitute and solve, often with a calculator or inside a real shape.
problem_bank.gold_description: Turn a worded or real situation into a right-angled triangle, then finish with Pythagoras or trigonometry, sometimes reaching into three dimensions.

worked_examples.question: A right triangle has legs 5 cm and 12 cm. Find the hypotenuse.
In a right triangle, the hypotenuse is 10 cm and one angle is 35°. Find the side opposite this angle to 1 d.p.
A ladder leans against a wall reaching 6 m high. The foot of the ladder is 2.5 m from the wall. Find the angle with the ground to 1 d.p.

bronze.title: Bronze: one formula, straight in
steps: Read the two known values straight off the triangle. No rearranging needed yet.
For Pythagoras, square both sides then add for the hypotenuse, or subtract then square root for a shorter side.
For a trig side you are given the ratio (like \(\sin 30° = 0.5\)): multiply the hypotenuse by it.

example.question: Find the hypotenuse: sides 6 cm and 8 cm.

silver.title: Silver: choose and rearrange
steps: Nothing is handed to you ready to use. First decide: Pythagoras (three sides, no angle) or a trig ratio (an angle is involved).
Pick the ratio that pairs your two sides: \(\sin\) for O and H, \(\cos\) for A and H, \(\tan\) for O and A. Rearrange to make the unknown the subject.
Real shapes count too: split an isosceles triangle down the middle, or read the diagonal of a rectangle as a hypotenuse.

example.question: Find the opposite side when \(\theta = 30°\) and the hypotenuse is 14 cm.

gold.title: Gold: build the triangle from the words
steps: The right triangle is hidden in a story, a real shape, or a solid. Sketch it and label the sides you are told.
Journeys give two legs (find the hypotenuse). Elevation and depression give an angle with a height and a distance (use \(\tan\)).
For a cuboid, the space diagonal uses all three edges: \(\sqrt{a^2 + b^2 + c^2}\).

example.question: A ship sails 9 km east then 12 km north. How far is it from the start?

steps.label: Set up
steps.content: The two legs are 9 and 12; the direct distance is the hypotenuse.

opener.label: Before any formula
opener.display: Short sides 3 and 4, a tiled square on every side.

steps.say: Here is a right-angled triangle with a square tiled onto each side. No formula needed, just count and add.
steps.pre: The two smaller squares hold 9 tiles and 16 tiles. Altogether that is 9 + 16 =
steps.hint: Just add the two tile counts.

steps.say: The clever bit: the square on the longest side holds exactly that many tiles too, 25. That is Pythagoras, the two smaller squares add up to the biggest one.
steps.pre: A square made of 25 tiles is how many tiles along each edge?

steps.say: So the longest side is 5. In symbols, the short sides \(a\) and \(b\) and the longest side \(c\) obey \(a^2 + b^2 = c^2\). Squaring a side counts the tiles in its square; square rooting turns the tile count back into a length.

bronze.label: Together: your first one
bronze.display: Find the hypotenuse of a right triangle with shorter sides 12 cm and 16 cm.

steps.say: The two shorter sides are 12 and 16. Pythagoras says: square each, add, then square root.

steps.pre: Square root to get the hypotenuse: √400 =
steps.hint: What number times itself makes 400? Try 20.
steps.done: Square, add, root. That is the whole method.

silver.label: Together: the silver move
silver.display: In a right triangle the opposite side is 9 cm and the adjacent side is 12 cm. Find the angle \(\theta\) to 1 d.p.

steps.say: You know the opposite and the adjacent, so the ratio is tan. To get the angle back, use inverse tan, the new move at this level.

steps.pre: Inverse tan turns that ratio into the angle: θ = tan⁻¹(0.75) =
steps.done: Inverse tan undoes tan to reveal the angle. That was the point.

steps.pre: The two acute angles add to 90°, so the other one is 90 − 36.9 =

steps.hint: Type tan(36.9) and round to 2 d.p.

gold.label: Together: the gold move
gold.display: A ramp rises 1.5 m over a horizontal run of 8 m. Find the angle the ramp makes with the ground, to 1 d.p.

steps.say: Draw the right triangle out of the words: the rise, 1.5 m, is opposite the angle; the run, 8 m, is adjacent. Opposite and adjacent means tan.

steps.pre: The ratio, rise ÷ run: 1.5 ÷ 8, to 2 d.p. =
Inverse tan gives the angle: θ = tan⁻¹(1.5 ÷ 8) =
steps.hint: Press tan⁻¹, then 1.5 ÷ 8; keep full accuracy.
steps.done: Reading the triangle out of the words is the gold move.

steps.hint: Type tan(10.6) and round to 2 d.p.
steps.done: 0.19 matches the ratio, so the ramp sits at 10.6°.

steps.pre: The ramp itself is the hypotenuse: √(1.5² + 8²) = √66.25, to 1 d.p. =
steps.hint: Square root of 66.25 on the calculator.
steps.done: Same triangle, Pythagoras gives the ramp's length: 8.1 m.
